questiontext.text:
A transfer fee method has a switch with a case per channel, and product managers add a channel every quarter.

Which refactoring best fits?

generalfeedback.text: Strategy keeps the calculator closed for modification and open for extension; Spring can inject all FeeRule beans as a list.

answer.text: Singleton: make the fee method static
Decorator: wrap the switch in another switch
Strategy: one FeeRule implementation per channel, collected by a calculator, so a new channel adds a class instead of editing the switch
Observer: publish an event for every fee

questiontext.text:
A service has a @Transactional method transferAll() that loops and calls this.transferOne(), also @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW). Each transfer was expected to commit separately, but they all roll back together.

Why?

generalfeedback.text: Spring applies @Transactional through a proxy around the bean. Self-invocation doesn't pass through the proxy; move transferOne() to another bean or use TransactionTemplate.

answer.text: REQUIRES_NEW is not supported by PostgreSQL
Loops can't run inside transactions
Calls through this bypass the Spring proxy, so transferOne()'s transaction settings are never applied
Spring creates a new proxy for every loop iteration

questiontext.text:
A QuoteService Spring bean stores private BigDecimal lastRate and sets it during each request. Customers occasionally see someone else's rate.

What is the cause?

generalfeedback.text: Singleton beans must be stateless or hold only thread-safe, immutable state. Keep per-request values in local variables or parameters.

answer.text: BigDecimal is not thread-safe for reading
Spring creates one bean per HTTP session by default
The JVM caches the field per user
Beans are singletons by default and shared by all request threads, so the field is shared mutable state

questiontext.text:
After a transfer commits, the bank must send an SMS, update a fraud score and refresh a dashboard, and new reactions are added often.

Which approach keeps the transfer service decoupled and safe?

generalfeedback.text: Observer via events decouples the publisher; the transactional listener avoids notifying about transfers that roll back.

answer.text: Use @EventListener so listeners run inside the transaction
Make the transfer service extend the SMS service
Publish a TransferCompleted application event and handle it with @TransactionalEventListener, which runs after commit
Call the three services directly at the start of the method

questiontext.text:
Your code calls a KYC vendor whose SDK returns VendorVerificationResponseV3 objects, and these types appear in controllers and repositories.

What should you introduce?

generalfeedback.text: Adapters keep third-party types at the edge, so switching vendors touches one class.

answer.text: A Builder for the vendor response
An Adapter implementing your own KycProvider interface that translates the vendor's types into your domain types
A Singleton wrapper around the SDK
A Template Method in the controller

questiontext.text:
Which of these are examples of the Template Method idea (a fixed algorithm with variable steps) in Spring? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Both templates run fixed steps (resources, exceptions, commit/rollback) and call your callback for the variable part.

answer.text: JdbcTemplate.query(sql, rowMapper)
@Value("${app.limit}")
TransactionTemplate.execute(status -> ...)
A record with a compact constructor

questiontext.text:
A record Transfer has nine components, four of them Strings, and tests keep passing arguments in the wrong order.

What improves construction most?

generalfeedback.text: Builders make many-argument construction readable and checkable while keeping the object immutable.

answer.text: Use a Map<String, Object> instead of a record
A Builder (hand-written or generated) or static factory methods with named steps, validating in build()
Make all fields public and mutable
Add a no-argument constructor and setters

questiontext.text:
A teammate adds an interface plus a factory for a class that has one implementation, no test double and no planned alternatives.

What is the best review comment?

generalfeedback.text: Patterns add indirection; introduce them when they solve a present problem.

answer.text: Approve, more interfaces are always better
Ask them to add an abstract base class as well
Ask for a Singleton too
Suggest removing the speculative abstraction until a second implementation or test need appears

questiontext.text:
A transfer fails with DataIntegrityViolationException; further down the trace is Caused by: PSQLException: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "journal_reference_key".

What is the most useful reading of this trace?

generalfeedback.text: The last Caused by is usually the root cause; your own first frame shows where your code was involved.

answer.text: The top line is always the root cause, so the problem is in Spring
Spring has a bug in its exception translation
The database is down
The root cause is a repeated journal reference hitting a unique constraint; find the first frame in your own package to see which call inserted it

questiontext.text:
A loop processes 20,000 transfers and fails only for reference TRF-2026-0193.

How do you stop the debugger exactly there?

generalfeedback.text: Conditional breakpoints suspend only when the expression is true.

answer.text: A conditional breakpoint with t.reference().equals("TRF-2026-0193")
Step over 20,000 times
Add Thread.sleep before the loop
Restart the IDE in safe mode

questiontext.text:
A service catches an exception somewhere deep in a library and returns null, so the error never reaches your logs.

Which debugger feature finds where it is thrown?

generalfeedback.text: Exception breakpoints stop where the exception is thrown, even if it is later caught.

answer.text: Evaluate Expression
A watch on a local variable
Drop Frame
An exception breakpoint on that exception type

questiontext.text:
Requests time out every afternoon. CPU is low. Three thread dumps taken ten seconds apart show most http-nio threads parked in HikariPool.getConnection.

What does this indicate?

generalfeedback.text: Threads waiting in getConnection mean connections aren't being returned fast enough.

answer.text: Garbage collection is too frequent
The JVM has run out of heap
The database connection pool is exhausted; find what holds connections for long (slow queries, long transactions, leaks) rather than only enlarging the pool
A deadlock between two HTTP threads

questiontext.text:
Heap use grows after every full GC until the service fails with OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space.

What is the best next step?

generalfeedback.text: Growing post-GC heap suggests a leak; the dominator tree shows which references keep objects alive.

answer.text: Capture a heap dump (or enable HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError) and inspect the dominator tree for what retains the memory
Switch to a different garbage collector
Double the heap and close the ticket
Restart the service every night

questiontext.text:
Which logging practices make production problems easier to solve? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Correlation ids link a request's lines; parameterised logs with the exception keep the stack trace. Sensitive data must never be logged.

answer.text: Putting a correlation id in the MDC for each request and returning it to the client
Logging full request bodies including card numbers
Logging with parameters and passing the exception as the last argument
Catching exceptions and logging only e.getMessage()

questiontext.text:
A teammate wants to enable JDWP remote debugging on the production server to investigate a bug quickly.

What is the right response?

generalfeedback.text: Remote debugging is for local or isolated environments; production needs safe diagnostics.

answer.text: Allow it and disable the firewall temporarily
Allow it during business hours only
Allow it if the port is changed from 5005
Refuse: an open debug port allows arbitrary code execution; reproduce locally, or use logs, metrics and dumps

questiontext.text:
A @Transactional method saves a statement header and then calls Files.readAllLines(file), which throws IOException. The header row stays in the database.

Why, and what is the fix?

generalfeedback.text: Checked exceptions commit by default; declare rollback rules explicitly when they must undo work.

answer.text: The method must be private
By default Spring rolls back only on unchecked exceptions; add rollbackFor = Exception.class (or IOException.class)
readOnly must be set to true
PostgreSQL ignores rollbacks for headers

questiontext.text:
An audit insert is marked @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW) and called from transfer() in the same class. When the transfer fails, the audit row disappears too.

Why?

generalfeedback.text: Self-invocation never reaches the proxy that would start the new transaction.

answer.text: REQUIRES_NEW only works with MongoDB
The call goes through this, bypassing the proxy, so the audit runs in the transfer's transaction; move it to a separate bean
Audit tables can't commit independently
The audit method needs @Async

questiontext.text:
An outer @Transactional method calls feeService.apply() (also @Transactional, default propagation), catches its RuntimeException and continues. On commit Spring throws UnexpectedRollbackException.

What happened?

generalfeedback.text: With REQUIRED both methods share one transaction; an inner failure marks it rollback-only.

answer.text: Spring can't catch RuntimeException
The database lost its connection
The inner method joined the same transaction and marked it rollback-only when it threw; catching the exception didn't undo that
Propagation REQUIRED always throws on commit

questiontext.text:
A singleton service has a prototype-scoped ReportBuilder injected through its constructor, expecting a fresh builder per request. Reports start mixing data.

What is wrong?

generalfeedback.text: Injection happens once; ask the container for a new prototype instance when you need one.

answer.text: Constructor injection is not allowed for prototypes
The prototype was injected once when the singleton was created; use ObjectProvider<ReportBuilder>.getObject() each time
Prototype beans are always thread-safe
Singletons are recreated per request

questiontext.text:
A nightly @Scheduled interest job is deployed on two pods behind a load balancer. Customers receive interest twice.

What is the best fix?

generalfeedback.text: Every instance runs every @Scheduled method; distributed locking plus idempotency prevents double posting.

answer.text: Add @Async to the job
Ensure only one instance runs it (ShedLock or a database advisory lock, or a platform scheduler) and make the job idempotent
Increase the scheduler thread pool
Change cron to fixedRate

questiontext.text:
A transfer service sends a confirmation SMS from an @EventListener. Some customers get SMSs for transfers that later rolled back.

What should change?

generalfeedback.text: Plain @EventListener runs synchronously inside the publisher's transaction.

answer.text: Send the SMS before saving
Use @TransactionalEventListener (AFTER_COMMIT) so the listener runs only after a successful commit
Use a prototype-scoped listener
Make the listener private

questiontext.text:
Which statements about Spring proxies are true? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Proxies wrap Spring-managed beans after initialisation and only intercept external calls to proxyable methods.

answer.text: Self-invocation always goes through the proxy
Proxies are created before the constructor runs
Annotations like @Transactional and @Cacheable don't apply to private methods
Objects created with new don't get Spring's proxy-based behaviour

questiontext.text:
A service is missing a DataSource at start-up after an upgrade, and the team can't tell why auto-configuration skipped it.

What is the quickest way to find out?

generalfeedback.text: The report lists which auto-configurations matched or didn't, and the condition responsible.

answer.text: Start with --debug (or the Actuator conditions endpoint) and read the conditions evaluation report
Switch to field injection
Delete the target folder
Add @ComponentScan everywhere

questiontext.text:
A JPA entity uses Lombok's @Data. Adding entities to a HashSet and then saving them makes the set behave strangely, and logs show a customer's BVN.

What is the problem?

generalfeedback.text: Use explicit equals/hashCode for entities and exclude sensitive fields from toString, or avoid @Data on entities.

answer.text: Lombok doesn't support HashSet
@Data generates equals/hashCode over all fields (including the generated id) and a toString that prints every field, including sensitive ones
The BVN field must be static
JPA entities can't have getters

questiontext.text:
A team uses MapStruct. A new field riskScore is added to the response DTO, but responses always show it as null and nothing failed.

What configuration would have caught this?

generalfeedback.text: MapStruct reports unmapped targets as warnings by default; making them errors catches missing mappings at compile time.

answer.text: componentModel = "default"
unmappedTargetPolicy = ReportingPolicy.ERROR, so unmapped target properties fail the build
Removing the mapper interface
Making the DTO a class instead of a record
